verdict.rationale: Nitrokey documents a PIV feature page and certificate-based login to computers and network services. Its docs also list Windows Login with Active Directory, OpenVPN and on-device key generation, so the core smart-card login story is present. However, the PIV evidence is only a page title, and Windows login and VPN are documented under the OpenPGP card feature rather than PIV. Missing for 10: substantive PIV documentation showing workstation sign-in and VPN via PIV, any code-signing evidence for the USB key (the only code-signing report concerns the separate Nitrokey HSM), explicit non-exportability guarantees, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, the key acts as a PIV smart card for certificate-based login — workstation sign-in, VPN, and code signing with keys that never leave the device
